approach: Fix at the source in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs. `Drain::attempts` ends an item whose last attempt fails, with no pause and no flag, as `ItemEnd::Failed` (drain.rs:1841); `Drain::finish` turns that into `set_stop(Stop::RepeatedFailure, ..)` (drain.rs:2426), which ends the whole batch. Change that arm to `pass_over(&item.job, "failed twice; left for the scope guard and Hestia: <last reason>")`, the call the Paused and Flagged arms make, so the next item runs. One thing the code showed that the first plan missed: the drain has no login stop of its own. An expired producer login closes the job as Failed with the reason `environment: producer login expired` (disk.rs:328, run/producer.rs:205-209, `StopCause::of` disk.rs:388). Environment stops do not count as spend on the scope guard's line (scope_guard.rs:78), so the line is never paused or flagged. Today such a job is retried once and then ends the batch only through `RepeatedFailure`. Deleting that arm without a replacement would let an expired login or usage limit run every queued item twice and drain the budget, which breaks the instruction to keep the login stop. So the same arm also checks the last failure's reason with `athena_core::disk::StopCause::of`. For `ProducerAuth`, `UsageLimit` and `LowDisk` it also calls `set_stop(Stop::Environment)` (the Budget arm's pass_over plus set_stop pattern). Those stops are about the machine or account, not the item. `Stop::RepeatedFailure` is replaced by `Stop::Environment` in the same place in `Stop::ALL`, which stays at 9. `Report.failed_item` and the failed-item half of `Drain.stop` are deleted, because no stop now names a single item. The help text, display special case, docs, README line, CHANGELOG and tests follow.

decisions.choice: The unflagged, unpaused double failure becomes a pass_over in the `ItemEnd::Failed` arm, with its own reason text 'failed twice; left for the scope guard and Hestia: <last reason>'. `ItemEnd::Failed` stays as the item end.
decisions.reason: `pass_over` (drain.rs:1391) records the item once per run, and the scope guard's and Hestia's inputs (the job lines and job records) are unchanged. The change is one match arm at the source of the fault.

rejected.option: Fold the case into ItemEnd::Flagged with a synthetic reason
rejected.why: It hides that no flag exists; `Flagged` is documented as the scope guard's flag.

rejected.option: Retry a third time before passing over
rejected.why: Out of scope: ATTEMPTS and the retry policy do not change.

decisions.choice: Keep a batch stop for failures that are not about the item: after the second failure, if `StopCause::of(last reason)` is ProducerAuth (expired login), UsageLimit or LowDisk, pass the item over and also `set_stop(Stop::Environment)`. Add `Stop::Environment` where `RepeatedFailure` was (label 'environment stopped', meaning that the login expired, a usage limit was reached or disk is low, so every later item would fail the same way; fix it and run the drain again). CheckTimeout and OtherEnvironment are not batch stops and are just passed over.
decisions.reason: This answers the brief's instruction to keep the login (and disk) stops. Reading the code shows they exist only because a Failed job with an environment reason reached the RepeatedFailure arm. `StopCause` is the one place that classifies closing reasons (disk.rs:358-366), so no word list is added. The check is one extra condition in the same arm.

rejected.why: An expired login or usage limit would run every queued item twice and spend the budget; the brief says to keep the login stop.

rejected.option: Keep Stop::RepeatedFailure and also check the reason
rejected.why: The name and help text would still say a single item's double failure stops the batch.

rejected.why: It changes retry behaviour; the retry policy is out of scope.

risks.risk: With no stop after a work failure, concurrent-stub tests that relied on the stop to end the run may run extra items and become order dependent.
risks.mitigation: The concurrent and matrix tests already order with `wait_for`. Run the drain tests twice, once with `-- --test-threads=1` and once with the default, and fix any ordering dependence by `wait_for`, not by sleeps.

risks.risk: The environment check misclassifies: a work failure whose reason text happens to match, or an environment failure whose reason is not on the job line, so the batch is not stopped.
risks.mitigation: `StopCause::of` is the single classifier and reads only the `environment:` prefix or an API error 401/429 in a producer-stop detail (disk.rs:343-409), not free prose. The drain reads the reason from `Run.reason`, which is the job's closing reason (`f.reason`, drain.rs:3607-3611). Tests cover the login, work-failure and check-timeout reasons.

risks.risk: Other test files may drain a failing item and expect the old stop (steward.rs, retry.rs).
risks.mitigation: Grep found no `drain::Stop` use outside drain.rs, display.rs, main.rs, tests/drain.rs and tests/job_plan.rs. The producer runs the full workspace tests; if a test needed the stop to end its drain, limit its queue to the failing item.

risks.risk: A batch with many failing work items now spends the whole budget instead of stopping at the first double failure.
risks.mitigation: This is the requested behaviour. Cost is still bounded by the budget and job-limit stops and by the scope guard's pause and flag on a thrashing line. The pass-over reason names the scope guard and Hestia.

It names the 4 Nov 12:39pm UTC stop of job 20261029-160024-80qj (with $43 and 3 job slots left) and the root cause: the item-end handler set `Stop::RepeatedFailure` for an item with no pause or flag. It also says the `repeated failure` stop and the report's `failed_item` key are removed, and that a failure caused by an expired login, usage limit or low disk still stops the batch, now as `environment stopped`. README.md:126 no longer says the run ends in `repeated failure`.
demonstrations.observes: The CHANGELOG entry carries the job id, the date and time, the root cause and the stop/key changes. README.md:126 describes the pass-over.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the edits the diff shows no CHANGELOG entry naming the job, and README.md:126 still says the run ends in `repeated failure`.
